metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: These are the words of Amos, who was among the sheepherders of Tekoa— what he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake, in the days when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel.
units.rightText: The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
leftNotes: 1:1 Hebrew Joash, a variant of Jehoash

units.leftText: He said: “The LORD roars from Zion and raises His voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers.”
units.rightText: And he said, Jehovah will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the pastures of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Carmel shall wither.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Damascus, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they threshed Gilead with sledges of iron.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: For three transgressions of Damascus, yea, for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron.
leftNotes: 1:3 Or I will not revoke the punishment; Hebrew I will not revoke it; also in verses 6, 9, 11, and 13

units.leftText: So I will send fire upon the house of Hazael to consume the citadels of Ben-hadad.
units.rightText: But I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, and it shall devour the palaces of Ben-hadad.

units.leftText: I will break down the gates of Damascus; I will cut off the ruler from the Valley of Aven and the one who wields the scepter in Beth-eden. The people of Aram will be exiled to Kir,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: And I will break the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the valley of Aven, and him that holdeth the sceptre from the house of Eden; and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Gaza, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they exiled a whole population, delivering them up to Edom.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: For three transgressions of Gaza, yea, for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they carried away captive the whole people, to deliver them up to Edom.

units.leftText: So I will send fire upon the walls of Gaza, to consume its citadels.
units.rightText: But I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, and it shall devour the palaces thereof.

units.leftText: I will cut off the ruler of Ashdod and the one who wields the scepter in Ashkelon. I will turn My hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish,” says the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him that holdeth the sceptre from Ashkelon; and I will turn my hand against Ekron; and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish, saith the Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Tyre, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they delivered up a whole congregation of exiles to Edom and broke a covenant of brotherhood.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: For three transgressions of Tyre, yea, for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole people to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant.

units.leftText: So I will send fire upon the walls of Tyre to consume its citadels.”
units.rightText: But I will send a fire on the wall of Tyre, and it shall devour the palaces thereof.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Edom, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because he pursued his brother with the sword and stifled all compassion; his anger raged continually, and his fury flamed incessantly.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: For three transgressions of Edom, yea, for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever.

units.leftText: So I will send fire upon Teman to consume the citadels of Bozrah.”
units.rightText: But I will send a fire upon Teman, and it shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of the Ammonites, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to enlarge their territory.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, yea, for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they may enlarge their border.

units.leftText: So I will kindle a fire in the walls of Rabbah to consume its citadels amid war cries on the day of battle and a violent wind on the day of tempest.
units.rightText: But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind;

units.leftText: Their king will go into exile — he and his princes together,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith Jehovah.
leftNotes: 1:15 Possibly Milcom will go into exile; Milcom, also called Molech, was god of the Ammonites; see Leviticus 18:21|LEV 18:21* and 1 Kings 11:7.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Moab, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because he burned to lime the bones of Edom’s king.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: For three transgressions of Moab, yea, for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime.
leftNotes: 2:1 Or I will not revoke the punishment; Hebrew I will not revoke it; also in verses 4 and 6

units.leftText: So I will send fire against Moab to consume the citadels of Kerioth. Moab will die in tumult, amid war cries and the sound of the ram’s horn.
units.rightText: But I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the palaces of Kerioth; and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet;

units.leftText: I will cut off the ruler of Moab and kill all the officials with him,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: and I will cut off the judge from the midst thereof, and will slay all the princes thereof with him, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Judah, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they reject the Law of the LORD and fail to keep His statutes; they are led astray by the lies in which their fathers walked.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: For three transgressions of Judah, yea, for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have rejected the law of Jehovah, and have not kept his statutes, and their lies have caused them to err, after which their fathers did walk.

units.leftText: So I will send fire upon Judah to consume the citadels of Jerusalem.”
units.rightText: But I will send a fire upon Judah, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Israel, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they sell the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: For three transgressions of Israel, yea, for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have sold the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes—

units.leftText: They trample on the heads of the poor as on the dust of the earth; they push the needy out of their way. A man and his father have relations with the same girl and so profane My holy name.
units.rightText: they that pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, and turn aside the way of the meek: and a man and his father go unto the same maiden, to profane my holy name:

units.leftText: They lie down beside every altar on garments taken in pledge. And in the house of their God, they drink wine obtained through fines.
units.rightText: and they lay themselves down beside every altar upon clothes taken in pledge; and in the house of their God they drink the wine of such as have been fined.
leftNotes: 2:8 Or they drink the wine of those who have been fined

units.leftText: Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, though his height was like that of the cedars, and he was as strong as the oaks. Yet I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
units.rightText: Yet destroyed I the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.

units.leftText: And I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you forty years in the wilderness, that you might take possession of the land of the Amorite.
units.rightText: Also I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and led you forty years in the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite.

units.leftText: I raised up prophets from your sons and Nazirites from your young men. Is this not true, O children of Israel?” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazirites. Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel? saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “But you made the Nazirites drink wine and commanded the prophets not to prophesy.
units.rightText: But ye gave the Nazirites wine to drink, and commanded the prophets, saying, Prophesy not.

units.leftText: Behold, I am about to crush you in your place as with a cart full of grain.
units.rightText: Behold, I will press you in your place, as a cart presseth that is full of sheaves.

units.leftText: Escape will fail the swift, the strong will not prevail by his strength, and the mighty will not save his life.
units.rightText: And flight shall perish from the swift; and the strong shall not strengthen his force; neither shall the mighty deliver himself;

units.leftText: The archer will not stand his ground, the fleet of foot will not escape, and the horseman will not save his life.
units.rightText: neither shall he stand that handleth the bow; and he that is swift of foot shall not deliver himself; neither shall he that rideth the horse deliver himself;

units.leftText: Even the bravest of mighty men will flee naked on that day,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: and he that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt:
units.rightText: Hear this word that Jehovah hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying,

units.leftText: “Only you have I known from all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.”
units.rightText: You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities.

units.leftText: Can two walk together without agreeing where to go?
units.rightText: Shall two walk together, except they have agreed?
leftNotes: 3:3 Or without an appointment to meet

units.leftText: Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Does a young lion growl in his den if he has caught nothing?
units.rightText: Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey? will a young lion cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing?

units.leftText: Does a bird land in a snare where no bait has been set? Does a trap spring from the ground when it has nothing to catch?
units.rightText: Can a bird fall in a snare upon the earth, where no gin is set for him? shall a snare spring up from the ground, and have taken nothing at all?

units.leftText: If a ram’s horn sounds in a city, do the people not tremble? If calamity comes to a city, has not the LORD caused it?
units.rightText: Shall the trumpet be blown in a city, and the people not be afraid? shall evil befall a city, and Jehovah hath not done it?

units.leftText: Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His plan to His servants the prophets.
units.rightText: Surely the Lord Jehovah will do nothing, except he reveal his secret unto his servants the prophets.

units.leftText: The lion has roared — who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken — who will not prophesy?
units.rightText: The lion hath roared; who will not fear? The Lord Jehovah hath spoken; who can but prophesy?

units.leftText: Proclaim to the citadels of Ashdod and to the citadels of Egypt: “Assemble on the mountains of Samaria; see the great unrest in the city and the acts of oppression in her midst.”
units.rightText: Publish ye in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say, Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold what great tumults are therein, and what oppressions in the midst thereof.

units.leftText: “For they know not how to do right,” declares the LORD. “They store up violence and destruction in their citadels.”
units.rightText: For they know not to do right, saith Jehovah, who store up violence and robbery in their palaces.

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: “An enemy will surround the land; he will pull down your strongholds and plunder your citadels.”
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah: An adversary there shall be, even round about the land; and he shall bring down thy strength from thee, and thy palaces shall be plundered.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “As the shepherd snatches from the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so the Israelites dwelling in Samaria will be rescued having just the corner of a bed or the cushion of a couch.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: As the shepherd rescueth out of the mouth of the lion two legs, or a piece of an ear, so shall the children of Israel be rescued that sit in Samaria in the corner of a couch, and on the silken cushions of a bed.
leftNotes: 3:12 Or so will the Israelites be snatched away, those who sit in Samaria on the edge of their beds and in Damascus on their couches

units.leftText: Hear and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord GOD, the God of Hosts.
units.rightText: Hear ye, and testify against the house of Jacob, saith the Lord Jehovah, the God of hosts.

units.leftText: On the day I punish Israel for their transgressions, I will visit destruction on the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be cut off, and they will fall to the ground.
units.rightText: For in the day that I shall visit the transgressions of Israel upon him, I will also visit the altars of Beth-el; and the horns of the altar shall be cut off, and fall to the ground.

units.leftText: I will tear down the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory will also perish, and the great houses will come to an end,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: And I will smite the winter-house with the summer-house; and the houses of ivory shall perish, and the great houses shall have an end, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on Mount Samaria, you women who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to your husbands, “Bring us more to drink.”
units.rightText: Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, that oppress the poor, that crush the needy, that say unto their lords, Bring, and let us drink.

units.leftText: The Lord GOD has sworn by His holiness: “Behold, the days are coming when you will be taken away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks.
units.rightText: The Lord Jehovah hath sworn by his holiness, that, lo, the days shall come upon you, that they shall take you away with hooks, and your residue with fish-hooks.

units.leftText: You will go out through broken walls, each one straight ahead of her, and you will be cast out toward Harmon, ” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: And ye shall go out at the breaches, every one straight before her; and ye shall cast yourselves into Harmon, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Go to Bethel and transgress; rebel even more at Gilgal! Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days.
units.rightText: Come to Beth-el, and transgress; to Gilgal, and multiply transgression; and bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes every three days;

units.leftText: Offer leavened bread as a thank offering, and loudly proclaim your freewill offerings. For that is what you children of Israel love to do,” declares the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: and offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving of that which is leavened, and proclaim freewill-offerings and publish them: for this pleaseth you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: “I afflicted all your cities with cleanness of teeth and all your towns with lack of bread, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: And I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places; yet have ye not returned unto me, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “I also withheld the rain from you when the harvest was three months away. I sent rain on one city but withheld it from another. One field received rain; another without rain withered.
units.rightText: And I also have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest; and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one piece was rained upon, and the piece whereupon it rained not withered.

units.leftText: People staggered from city to city for water to drink, but they were not satisfied; yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: So two or three cities wandered unto one city to drink water, and were not satisfied: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “I struck you with blight and mildew in your growing gardens and vineyards; the locust devoured your fig and olive trees, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: the multitude of your gardens and your vineyards and your fig-trees and your olive-trees hath the palmer-worm devoured: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “I sent plagues among you like those of Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, along with your captured horses. I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camp, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt: your young men have I slain with the sword, and have carried away your horses; and I have made the stench of your camp to come up even into your nostrils: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Some of you I overthrew as I overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a firebrand snatched from a blaze, yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: I have overthrown cities among you, as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and ye were as a brand plucked out of the burning: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Therefore, that is what I will do to you, O Israel, and since I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, O Israel!
units.rightText: Therefore thus will I do unto thee, O Israel; and because I will do this unto thee, prepare to meet thy God, O Israel.

units.leftText: For behold, He who forms the mountains, who creates the wind and reveals His thoughts to man, who turns the dawn to darkness and strides on the heights of the earth— the LORD, the God of Hosts, is His name.”
units.rightText: For, lo, he that formeth the mountains, and createth the wind, and declareth unto man what is his thought; that maketh the morning darkness, and treadeth upon the high places of the earth—Jehovah, the God of hosts, is his name.

units.leftText: Hear this word, O house of Israel, this lamentation I take up against you:
units.rightText: Hear ye this word which I take up for a lamentation over you, O house of Israel.

units.leftText: “Fallen is Virgin Israel, never to rise again. She lies abandoned on her land, with no one to raise her up.”
units.rightText: The virgin of Israel is fallen; she shall no more rise: she is cast down upon her land; there is none to raise her up.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD says: “The city that marches out a thousand strong will have but a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred strong will have but ten left in the house of Israel.” A Call to Repentance (Joel 1:13–20|JOL 1:13-20*; Zephaniah 2:1–3|ZEP 2:1-3*; Luke 13:1–5|LUK 13:1-5*)
units.rightText: For thus saith the Lord Jehovah: The city that went forth a thousand shall have a hundred left, and that which went forth a hundred shall have ten left, to the house of Israel.

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: “Seek Me and live!
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah unto the house of Israel, Seek ye me, and ye shall live;

units.leftText: Do not seek Bethel or go to Gilgal; do not journey to Beersheba, for Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.
units.rightText: but seek not Beth-el, nor enter into Gilgal, and pass not to Beer-sheba: for Gilgal shall surely go into captivity, and Beth-el shall come to nought.
leftNotes: 5:5 Hebrew to Aven, a reference to Beth-aven, a derogatory term for Bethel; see Hosea 4:15|HOS 4:15*.

units.leftText: Seek the LORD and live, or He will sweep like fire through the house of Joseph; it will devour everything, with no one at Bethel to extinguish it.
units.rightText: Seek Jehovah, and ye shall live; lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and it devour, and there be none to quench it in Beth-el.

units.leftText: There are those who turn justice into wormwood and cast righteousness to the ground.
units.rightText: Ye who turn justice to wormwood, and cast down righteousness to the earth,

units.leftText: He who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns darkness into dawn and darkens day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth — the LORD is His name —
units.rightText: seek him that maketh the Pleiades and Orion, and turneth the shadow of death into the morning, and maketh the day dark with night; that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth (Jehovah is his name);

units.leftText: He flashes destruction on the strong, so that fury comes upon the stronghold.
units.rightText: that bringeth sudden destruction upon the strong, so that destruction cometh upon the fortress.

units.leftText: There are those who hate the one who reproves in the gate and despise him who speaks with integrity.
units.rightText: They hate him that reproveth in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.

units.leftText: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and exact from him a tax of grain, you will never live in the stone houses you have built; you will never drink the wine from the lush vineyards you have planted.
units.rightText: Forasmuch therefore as ye trample upon the poor, and take exactions from him of wheat: ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink the wine thereof.

units.leftText: For I know that your transgressions are many and your sins are numerous. You oppress the righteous by taking bribes; you deprive the poor of justice in the gate.
units.rightText: For I know how manifold are your transgressions, and how mighty are your sins—ye that afflict the just, that take a bribe, and that turn aside the needy in the gate from their right.

units.leftText: Therefore, the prudent keep silent in such times, for the days are evil.
units.rightText: Therefore he that is prudent shall keep silence in such a time; for it is an evil time.

units.leftText: Seek good, not evil, so that you may live. And the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be with you, as you have claimed.
units.rightText: Seek good, and not evil, that ye may live; and so Jehovah, the God of hosts, will be with you, as ye say.

units.leftText: Hate evil and love good; establish justice in the gate. Perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.” Woe to Rebellious Israel (Acts 7:39–43|ACT 7:39-43*)
units.rightText: Hate the evil, and love the good, and establish justice in the gate: it may be that Jehovah, the God of hosts, will be gracious unto the remnant of Joseph.

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Hosts, the Lord, says: “There will be wailing in all the public squares and cries of ‘Alas! Alas!’ in all the streets. The farmer will be summoned to mourn, and the mourners to wail.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith Jehovah, the God of hosts, the Lord: Wailing shall be in all the broad ways; and they shall say in all the streets, Alas! alas! and they shall call the husbandman to mourning, and such as are skilful in lamentation to wailing.

units.leftText: There will be wailing in all the vineyards, for I will pass through your midst,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: And in all vineyards shall be wailing; for I will pass through the midst of thee, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: Woe to you who long for the Day of the LORD! What will the Day of the LORD be for you? It will be darkness and not light.
units.rightText: Woe unto you that desire the day of Jehovah! Wherefore would ye have the day of Jehovah? It is darkness, and not light.

units.leftText: It will be like a man who flees from a lion, only to encounter a bear, or who enters his house and rests his hand against the wall, only to be bitten by a snake.
units.rightText: As if a man did flee from a lion, and a bear met him; or went into the house and leaned his hand on the wall, and a serpent bit him.

units.leftText: Will not the Day of the LORD be darkness and not light, even gloom with no brightness in it?
units.rightText: Shall not the day of Jehovah be darkness, and not light? even very dark, and no brightness in it?

units.leftText: “I hate, I despise your feasts! I cannot stand the stench of your solemn assemblies.
units.rightText: I hate, I despise your feasts, and I will take no delight in your solemn assemblies.

units.leftText: Even though you offer Me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them; for your peace offerings of fattened cattle I will have no regard.
units.rightText: Yea, though ye offer me your burnt-offerings and meal-offerings, I will not accept them; neither will I regard the peace-offerings of your fat beasts.

units.leftText: Take away from Me the noise of your songs! I will not listen to the music of your harps.
units.rightText: Take thou away from me the noise of thy songs; for I will not hear the melody of thy viols.

units.leftText: But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
units.rightText: But let justice roll down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

units.leftText: Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
units.rightText: Did ye bring unto me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, O house of Israel?

units.leftText: You have taken along Sakkuth your king and Kaiwan your star god, the idols you made for yourselves.
units.rightText: Yea, ye have borne the tabernacle of your king and the shrine of your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.
leftNotes: 5:26 LXX You have taken along the tabernacle of Molech and the star of your god Rephan

units.leftText: Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Damascus,” says the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts.
units.rightText: Therefore will I cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus, saith Jehovah, whose name is the God of hosts.

units.leftText: Woe to those at ease in Zion and those secure on Mount Samaria, the distinguished ones of the foremost nation, to whom the house of Israel comes.
units.rightText: Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and to them that are secure in the mountain of Samaria, the notable men of the chief of the nations, to whom the house of Israel come!

units.leftText: Cross over to Calneh and see; go from there to the great Hamath; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?
units.rightText: Pass ye unto Calneh, and see; and from thence go ye to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines: are they better than these kingdoms? or is their border greater than your border?

units.leftText: You dismiss the day of calamity and bring near a reign of violence.
units.rightText: —ye that put far away the evil day, and cause the seat of violence to come near;

units.leftText: You lie on beds inlaid with ivory, and lounge upon your couches. You dine on lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.
units.rightText: that lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the midst of the stall;

units.leftText: You improvise songs on the harp like David and invent your own musical instruments.
units.rightText: that sing idle songs to the sound of the viol; that invent for themselves instruments of music, like David;

units.leftText: You drink wine by the bowlful and anoint yourselves with the finest oils, but you fail to grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
units.rightText: that drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief oils; but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.

units.leftText: Therefore, you will now go into exile as the first of the captives, and your feasting and lounging will come to an end. The Pride of Israel
units.rightText: Therefore shall they now go captive with the first that go captive; and the revelry of them that stretched themselves shall pass away.

units.leftText: The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself— the LORD, the God of Hosts, has declared: “I abhor Jacob’s pride and detest his citadels, so I will deliver up the city and everything in it.”
units.rightText: The Lord Jehovah hath sworn by himself, saith Jehovah, the God of hosts: I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces; therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein.

units.leftText: And if there are ten men left in one house, they too will die.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, if there remain ten men in one house, that they shall die.

units.leftText: And when the relative who is to burn the bodies picks them up to remove them from the house, he will call to one inside, “Is anyone else with you?” “None,” that person will answer. “Silence,” the relative will retort, “for the name of the LORD must not be invoked.”
units.rightText: And when a man’s uncle shall take him up, even he that burneth him, to bring out the bones out of the house, and shall say unto him that is in the innermost parts of the house, Is there yet any with thee? and he shall say, No; then shall he say, Hold thy peace; for we may not make mention of the name of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 6:10 Or to make a funeral fire to honor the dead

units.leftText: For the LORD gives a command: “The great house will be smashed to pieces, and the small house to rubble.”
units.rightText: For, behold, Jehovah commandeth, and the great house shall be smitten with breaches, and the little house with clefts.

units.leftText: “Do horses gallop on the cliffs? Does one plow the sea with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood—
units.rightText: Shall horses run upon the rock? will one plow there with oxen? that ye have turned justice into gall, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood;

units.leftText: you who rejoice in Lo-debar and say, ‘Did we not take Karnaim by our own strength?’
units.rightText: ye that rejoice in a thing of nought, that say, Have we not taken to us horns by our own strength?
leftNotes: 6:13 Karnaim means horn, a symbol of strength.

units.leftText: For behold, I will raise up a nation against you, O house of Israel,” declares the LORD, the God of Hosts, “and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.”
units.rightText: For, behold, I will raise up against you a nation, O house of Israel, saith Jehovah, the God of hosts; and they shall afflict you from the entrance of Hamath unto the brook of the Arabah.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: He was preparing swarms of locusts just after the king’s harvest, as the late spring crop was coming up.
units.rightText: Thus the Lord Jehovah showed me: and, behold, he formed locusts in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and, lo, it was the latter growth after the king’s mowings.
leftNotes: 7:1 LXX A swarm of locusts coming from the east; and, behold, one grasshopper, king Gog.

units.leftText: And when the locusts had eaten every green plant in the land, I said, “Lord GOD, please forgive! How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass that, when they made an end of eating the grass of the land, then I said, O Lord Jehovah, forgive, I beseech thee: how shall Jacob stand? for he is small.

units.leftText: So the LORD relented from this plan. “It will not happen,” He said.
units.rightText: Jehovah repented concerning this: It shall not be, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: The Lord GOD was calling for judgment by fire. It consumed the great deep and devoured the land.
units.rightText: Thus the Lord Jehovah showed me: and, behold, the Lord Jehovah called to contend by fire; and it devoured the great deep, and would have eaten up the land.

units.leftText: Then I said, “Lord GOD, please stop! How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?”
units.rightText: Then said I, O Lord Jehovah, cease, I beseech thee: how shall Jacob stand? for he is small.

units.leftText: So the LORD relented from this plan. “It will not happen either,” said the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: Jehovah repented concerning this: This also shall not be, saith the Lord Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is what He showed me: Behold, the Lord was standing by a wall true to plumb, with a plumb line in His hand.
units.rightText: Thus he showed me: and, behold, the Lord stood beside a wall made by a plumb-line, with a plumb-line in his hand.

units.leftText: “Amos, what do you see?” asked the LORD. “A plumb line,” I replied. “Behold,” said the Lord, “I am setting a plumb line among My people Israel; I will no longer spare them:
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto me, Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A plumb-line. Then said the Lord, Behold, I will set a plumb-line in the midst of my people Israel; I will not again pass by them any more;

units.leftText: The high places of Isaac will be deserted, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste; and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with My sword.” Amaziah Accuses Amos
units.rightText: and the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.

units.leftText: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land cannot bear all his words,
units.rightText: Then Amaziah the priest of Beth-el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.

units.leftText: for this is what Amos has said: ‘Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland.’”
units.rightText: For thus Amos saith, Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.

units.leftText: And Amaziah said to Amos, “Go away, you seer! Flee to the land of Judah; earn your bread there and do your prophesying there.
units.rightText: Also Amaziah said unto Amos, O thou seer, go, flee thou away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there:

units.leftText: But never prophesy at Bethel again, because it is the sanctuary of the king and the temple of the kingdom.”
units.rightText: but prophesy not again any more at Beth-el; for it is the king’s sanctuary, and it is a royal house.

units.leftText: “I was not a prophet,” Amos replied, “nor was I the son of a prophet; rather, I was a herdsman and a tender of sycamore-fig trees.
units.rightText: Then answered Amos, and said to Amaziah, I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was a herdsman, and a dresser of sycomore-trees:
leftNotes: 7:14 Or nor am I the son

units.leftText: But the LORD took me from following the flock and said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’
units.rightText: and Jehovah took me from following the flock, and Jehovah said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.

units.leftText: Now, therefore, hear the word of the LORD. You say: ‘Do not prophesy against Israel; do not preach against the house of Isaac.’
units.rightText: Now therefore hear thou the word of Jehovah: Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not thy word against the house of Isaac;

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the LORD says: ‘Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, and your sons and daughters will fall by the sword. Your land will be divided by a measuring line, and you yourself will die on pagan soil. And Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland.’”
units.rightText: therefore thus saith Jehovah: Thy wife shall be a harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou thyself shalt die in a land that is unclean, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.

units.leftText: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: I saw a basket of summer fruit.
units.rightText: Thus the Lord Jehovah showed me: and, behold, a basket of summer fruit.
leftNotes: 8:1 Or ripe fruit; also in verse 2

units.leftText: “Amos, what do you see?” He asked. “A basket of summer fruit,” I replied. So the LORD said to me, “The end has come for My people Israel; I will no longer spare them.”
units.rightText: And he said, Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A basket of summer fruit. Then said Jehovah unto me, The end is come upon my people Israel; I will not again pass by them any more.

units.leftText: “In that day,” declares the Lord GOD, “the songs of the temple will turn to wailing. Many will be the corpses, strewn in silence everywhere!”
units.rightText: And the songs of the temple shall be wailings in that day, saith the Lord Jehovah: the dead bodies shall be many; in every place shall they cast them forth with silence.

units.leftText: Hear this, you who trample the needy, who do away with the poor of the land,
units.rightText: Hear this, O ye that would swallow up the needy, and cause the poor of the land to fail,

units.leftText: asking, “When will the New Moon be over, that we may sell grain? When will the Sabbath end, that we may market wheat? Let us reduce the ephah and increase the shekel; let us cheat with dishonest scales.
units.rightText: saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell grain? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and dealing falsely with balances of deceit;
leftNotes: 8:5 Or Let us reduce the measure and increase the price

units.leftText: Let us buy the poor with silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, selling even the chaff with the wheat!”
units.rightText: that we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes, and sell the refuse of the wheat?

units.leftText: The LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: “I will never forget any of their deeds.
units.rightText: Jehovah hath sworn by the excellency of Jacob, Surely I will never forget any of their works.

units.leftText: Will not the land quake for this, and all its dwellers mourn? All of it will swell like the Nile; it will surge and then subside like the Nile in Egypt.
units.rightText: Shall not the land tremble for this, and every one mourn that dwelleth therein? yea, it shall rise up wholly like the River; and it shall be troubled and sink again, like the River of Egypt.

units.leftText: And in that day, declares the Lord GOD, I will make the sun go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the daytime.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord Jehovah, that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day.

units.leftText: I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into lamentation. I will cause everyone to wear sackcloth and every head to be shaved. I will make it like a time of mourning for an only son, and its outcome like a bitter day.
units.rightText: And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will bring sackcloth upon all loins, and baldness upon every head; and I will make it as the mourning for an only son, and the end thereof as a bitter day.

units.leftText: Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord GOD, when I will send a famine on the land — not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD.
units.rightText: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord Jehovah, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of Jehovah.

units.leftText: People will stagger from sea to sea and roam from north to east, seeking the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.
units.rightText: And they shall wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east; they shall run to and fro to seek the word of Jehovah, and shall not find it.

units.leftText: In that day the lovely young women — the young men as well — will faint from thirst.
units.rightText: In that day shall the fair virgins and the young men faint for thirst.

units.leftText: Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, ‘As surely as your god lives, O Dan,’ or, ‘As surely as the way of Beersheba lives’— they will fall, never to rise again.”
units.rightText: They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, As thy god, O Dan, liveth; and, As the way of Beer-sheba liveth; they shall fall, and never rise up again.

units.leftText: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said: “Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake. Topple them on the heads of all the people, and I will kill the rest with the sword. None of those who flee will get away; none of the fugitives will escape.
units.rightText: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar: and he said, Smite the capitals, that the thresholds may shake; and break them in pieces on the head of all of them; and I will slay the last of them with the sword: there shall not one of them flee away, and there shall not one of them escape.

units.leftText: Though they dig down to Sheol, from there My hand will take them; and though they climb up to heaven, from there I will pull them down.
units.rightText: Though they dig into Sheol, thence shall my hand take them; and though they climb up to heaven, thence will I bring them down.

units.leftText: Though they hide themselves atop Carmel, there I will track them and seize them; and though they hide from Me at the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent to bite them.
units.rightText: And though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them out thence; and though they be hid from my sight in the bottom of the sea, thence will I command the serpent, and it shall bite them.
leftNotes: 9:3 Hebrew nachash; translated in most cases as snake

units.leftText: Though they are driven by their enemies into captivity, there I will command the sword to slay them. I will fix My eyes upon them for harm and not for good.”
units.rightText: And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them: and I will set mine eyes upon them for evil, and not for good.

units.leftText: The Lord GOD of Hosts, He who touches the earth and it melts, and all its dwellers mourn — all the land rises like the Nile, then sinks like the river of Egypt —
units.rightText: For the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, is he that toucheth the land and it melteth, and all that dwell therein shall mourn; and it shall rise up wholly like the River, and shall sink again, like the River of Egypt;

units.leftText: He builds His upper rooms in the heavens and founds His vault upon the earth. He summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth. The LORD is His name.
units.rightText: it is he that buildeth his chambers in the heavens, and hath founded his vault upon the earth; he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth; Jehovah is his name.

units.leftText: “Are you not like the Cushites to Me, O children of Israel?” declares the LORD. “Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir?
units.rightText: Are ye not as the children of the Ethiopians unto me, O children of Israel? saith Jehovah. Have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?
leftNotes: 9:7 That is, people from the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Surely the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the earth. Yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Behold, the eyes of the Lord Jehovah are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth; save that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “For surely I will give the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as grain is sifted in a sieve; but not a pebble will reach the ground.
units.rightText: For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all the nations, like as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least kernel fall upon the earth.

units.leftText: All the sinners among My people will die by the sword — all those who say, ‘Disaster will never draw near or confront us.’” A Promise of Restoration (Acts 15:5–21|ACT 15:5-21*)
units.rightText: All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, who say, The evil shall not overtake nor meet us.

units.leftText: “In that day I will restore the fallen tent of David. I will repair its gaps, restore its ruins, and rebuild it as in the days of old,
units.rightText: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old;

units.leftText: that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name,” declares the LORD, who will do this.
units.rightText: that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and all the nations that are called by my name, saith Jehovah that doeth this.
leftNotes: 9:12 Hebrew; LXX that the remnant of men, and all the nations that bear My name, may earnestly seek Me; cited in Acts 15:16–18|ACT 15:16-18*

units.leftText: “Behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when the plowman will overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes, the sower of seed. The mountains will drip with sweet wine, with which all the hills will flow.
units.rightText: Behold, the days come, saith Jehovah, that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt.

units.leftText: I will restore My people Israel from captivity; they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
units.rightText: And I will bring back the captivity of my people Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and drink the wine thereof; they shall also make gardens, and eat the fruit of them.
leftNotes: 9:14 Or restore the fortunes of My people Israel

units.leftText: I will firmly plant them in their own land, never again to be uprooted from the land that I have given them,” says the LORD your God.
units.rightText: And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be plucked up out of their land which I have given them, saith Jehovah thy God.
